What is the difference between map(), filter() and reduce()?

Supplied answer
map(func, iterable) applies the function to every item and returns all results. filter(func, iterable) returns
only the items for which the function returns True. reduce(func, iterable) from functools combines all
items into one single value, for example a total. map and filter return lazy iterators in Python 3, so wrap
them in list().
